Q1: Aluminum chloride exhibits several Tier 1 (known) hazards, including carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, and reproductive hazards (CMR), environmental toxicity (ENV), oral toxicity (ORL), dermal and eye hazards (SKN), and organ and systemic hazards (OGN). It also presents Tier 2 (expanded perspective) inhalation hazards. Data regarding endocrine disruption (EDC) is currently deficient (Tier 4).
Q2: Aluminum chloride does not appear on any "Lists of Concern" or "Lists of Low Hazard."
Q3: Aluminum chloride is extensively studied, with 78,000 literature references, and is a well-defined small molecule. It has a moderate number of toxicity records (39), but has not undergone formal, comprehensive toxicological assessments by the EPA's IRIS or PPRTV programs.
